claims.text: Random mixing of elements with different atomic sizes and bonding characteristics produces a heterogeneous lattice-strain field in high-entropy or multi-principal-element alloys.
Heterogeneous lattice strain governs hardness and strength in high-entropy alloys.
Heterogeneous lattice strain promotes unusual dislocation behavior.
Heterogeneous lattice strain increases the formation of dislocation kinks and jogs.
Heterogeneous lattice strain increases bidirectional cross-slip.
The heterogeneous lattice-strain field contains localized regions of high internal stress.
Strain-induced unusual dislocation behavior pins dislocations and impedes dislocation glide.
Impeded dislocation glide produces increased hardness and strength.
Rapid solidification can increase disorder or heterogeneous lattice strain in an otherwise compositionally unchanged high-entropy alloy.
Cold working can increase disorder or heterogeneous lattice strain in an otherwise compositionally unchanged high-entropy alloy.
Annealing can homogenize the lattice and reduce local strain heterogeneity.
At otherwise controlled conditions, samples with greater heterogeneous lattice strain will have higher hardness than lower-heterogeneity samples.
At otherwise controlled conditions, samples with greater heterogeneous lattice strain will have higher yield strength than lower-heterogeneity samples.
Samples with greater heterogeneous lattice strain will show more frequent and complex kinks, jogs, and cross-slip events.
An untreated baseline will exhibit more conventional dislocation dynamics and fewer abnormal kink, jog, and cross-slip events.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to alloys whose constituent elements differ significantly in atomic size and bonding.
The mechanism may cease to govern strength when grain-boundary strengthening or precipitation dominates.
The mechanism may not be observable when the measurement scale fails to capture mesoscopic strain variations.
Discrete dislocation-dynamics simulations can explore dynamic dislocation evolution when the heterogeneous lattice-strain field is included.
A lack of both mechanical-property reduction and dislocation-behavior change in the nominally homogenized samples would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: Cold working and rapid solidification are proposed as ways to vary lattice strain while isolating it from other microstructural factors, but these treatments can also change dislocation density, grain structure, texture, segregation, and phase state. The stated design does not specify controls that separate these changes from the intended strain-field change.
